observations.seen: Untextured box buildings and a flat road. No street furniture density, signage, or skyline silhouette. Black in 2/3 desktop frames.
Van and jersey barriers are credible authored assets. Everything else is primitives or extrusions.
Barriers are textured. Buildings and road read as flat color with no detail maps.
Everything is matte or emissive. No car paint, glass, wet asphalt, or metal response.
No roughness variation, no specular highlights, no energy-plausible response. Emissive values are wildly over-driven.
Pure emissive-driven night with no motivated key light. The van is lit by its own bloom rather than the scene.
No visible cast shadows from van, barriers, or buildings. Objects float.
Flat navy ambient. No AO or contact darkening, and edges crush to black.
No env map and no road or vehicle reflections, which is the single biggest miss for a neon-night driving game.
Hard white clipping on the van and road lines while the rest is crushed. Exposure is mismanaged.
The palette (navy/teal/orange/cyan) is coherent in intent. Saturation dies in the clipped highlights.
Edges look acceptable at 1080p through JPEG. Bloom hides most aliasing.
Bloom threshold is far too low, so bloom swallows the hero object. No vignette, grading, or motion blur visible.
The pickup ring is clean but basic. Cyan side bars and the nav arrow are flat. No exhaust, sparks, or speed lines.
None visible in any frame.
No visible suspension, body roll, wheel steer, or lean cues. Desktop frames show no evidence of motion at all.
The player vehicle, the de facto character, is a white blob on desktop and a half-blown-out shape on mobile.
Desktop is too steep and high, which flattens the scene. Mobile is too close, so you cannot see the road ahead. Desktop camera likely the source of the black frames.
The road reads as a lane, but the blown centerline cuts the frame in half. Edges are dead black and there is no focal hierarchy.
Without fog, shadows, or texture detail, buildings have no readable scale. The distant bloom wall flattens depth.
No fog, haze, rain, volumetric light cones, or sky.
Pickup ring and parcel read on the one working desktop frame. Black frames score 0, and on mobile the HUD covers the road ahead.
Clean, consistent glass panels with good hierarchy on desktop. Mobile placement is poor.
Legible modern sans with good weight contrast. Desktop control hints are too small.
No screen shake, speed FX, or impact feedback visible. The delivery toast is the only feedback.
Renders, unlike desktop, but the camera is too tight and the HUD occludes key playfield areas.
One mediocre frame plus two black frames on the primary platform. Even the working frame is roughly a 3.5.
